statement: Removing a finding is not neutral when a criterion's status falls back to its score band. v26 item 6 made A5's no-reconciliation finding abstain; A5 has no calibrated status rule, so on every corpus specimen scored 1.4 the status moved from warning to critical at an unchanged score, and the scorer synthesized a metric-derived critical finding in its place. The tests written for the item checked the finding and the metrics and passed; only a full before/after report diff showed it. Rule: when a change adds or removes findings, diff each criterion's status and synthesized findings across the corpus, not just the finding you meant to change.

Read every count in a changelog entry back from the measurement output before committing it. A draft entry said six corpus specimens gained the A2 disclosure sentence; reading the comparison file showed two. The six came from scanning a mixed list of corpus and synthetic results by eye. Rule: each number written into a record is checked against the file it came from, filtered to the population the sentence names.
